newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia restricts foreign cargo to Batam.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia restricts foreign cargo to Batam.

text.p: Overseas cargo aircraft arrivals to Indonesia will be restricted to Hang Nadim airport on Batam Island despite requests by foreign operators for access to other airports in the country, an industry source said on Wednesday.

The source, who declined to be identified, told Reuters that foreign cargo carriers had asked for permission to operate out of Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta international airport but had been told they would only be allowed to fly to Batam, 20 km south of Singapore.
The carriers were still negotiating to use Jakarta, however, as Batam was not yet suitable for their operations, the source said.
"There are more connecting flights out of Jakarta than out of Batam," the source said. "Batam is not ready yet."
The official Antara news agency quoted Transport Minister Haryanto Dhanutirto as saying on Wednesday that the government's stance on Batam remained unchanged.

"I have rejected requests from cargo carriers such as Federal Express, United Parcel Service (UPS) and TNT (Express Worldwide) to serve Indonesia through other airports," Haryanto was quoted as saying.
"They may only land at Batam's Hang Nadim airport," he added.
The minister did not say when the ruling was to come into effect.

Indonesia has said it plans to develop Batam as a cargo hub to rival Singapore's Changi airport. Lower landing fee costs would make it more attractive to cargo operators, Haryanto was quoted as saying by Antara.
But the industry source said that Batam had far to go before it could threaten Singapore, where his company's Asian operations were based.
"It's already 10 years Batam has been in the news and it doesn't seem to be taking off...to such an extent that many developers are unwilling to move in there," the source said.
He said that if the government continues to refuse his company access to Jakarta then it will negotiate to fly to Denpasar airport on the holiday resort island of Bali instead.
The ruling comes after the launch earlier this week of Indonesian national airline Garuda's first aircraft specially dedicated to domestic cargo services.
The Boeing 737-200C will serve domestic routes in eastern Indonesia and operate from the country's second city Surabaya.
A second plane, which will begin operations next week, will serve western Indonesia and be based on Batam Island.
Haryanto was quoted as saying that foreign cargo operators will be able to fly freely to Batam but for other destinations in Indonesia they will have to use domestic carriers.
